title: Founding Software Engineer
quote: Probably pulled a '997' (outdoing the infamous 996), but honestly loved every moment in such a fast-paced environment with brilliant, relentless founders!
missions: Architected a document-parsing pipeline to replace manual labeling, converting unstructured educational content into structured Q&A data, which achieved ~83% conversion rate, accurately populating 10k+ questions.
Developed a video generation pipeline using LangGraph + Flutter that transforms students' graded performance into personalised, step-by-step explainer videos to address student's misconceptions.

Defined SLOs and cost projections for GenAI workloads; owned entire document-parsing features roadmap to raise extraction quality and extend coverage across subjects, curricula, languages, and modalities.

title: Generative AI Researcher Intern
quote: Was shocked to find our original engine would take centuries to generate the dataset we needed, but we pulled through... An awesome virgin experience to multimodal AI research!
missions: [MANUSCRIPT IN PREPARATION] SynDORBench: Benchmarking Human Detection and Action Recognition with DORI-Calibrated Distances.

Engineered a scalable synthetic-data engine using open-source datasets (SMPL-X, AMASS, and BABEL) and implemented an auto-labeling mechanism (pose/bbox/mask), which accelerates CV/VLM data collection.
Developed a DORI-aligned surveillance dataset (200k+ images & 630k+ QA pairs) with controlled context parameters to enable robust benchmarking of presence & action recognition models.
Built a unified evaluation framework for human-presence & action recognition, with Hydra configs and Docker/CUDA to benchmark YOLO models against compact LVLMs.

title: Algorithm Engineer Intern
quote: Easily the highlight of my undergraduate journey, got to work in a foreign country with awesome people and some seriously cool technology!
missions: Improved perception validation accuracy by 67% in large-scale environments through high-fidelity People Flow Monitoring simulations with realistic crowd dynamics and stochastic destination assignments (UE4/CARLA).
Supported pre-deployment validation of over 300 LiDARs across multiple terminals at a major SEA airport.

Cut simulation setup time by over 90% via an end-to-end scenario tooling suite for scenario configuration, point-cloud dataset generation, and fixed-seed regression checks, accelerating iteration velocity for algorithm team.

title: Computer Vision Engineer Intern
quote: Experienced the pain of working with a new symbolic computation library with very few documentation. Great learning curve and definitely not for the weak!
missions: Increased drone navigation accuracy by 20% in low-light, high-speed conditions by developing an Event-based Stereo Visual Odometry (ESVO) system using C++.
Achieved 5x latency reduction in state estimation (80%↓) by re-implementing non-linear solvers with SymForce symbolic computations, enabling real-time control feedback in drone navigation systems.

title: Student Trainee
quote: Working underwater taught me that failure modes are everywhere. When GPS doesn't work, you learn to rely on sound. When sensors fail, you build redundancy. Resilience isn't optional.
missions: Developed and tuned a three-hydrophone acoustic-localization system, boosting mission navigation accuracy by 40%.
Contributed across perception, hardware integration, and signal-processing tasks in the AUV development lifecycle.

title: Radio Frequency Engineer Intern
quote: Probably the only person to say that I have built a drone jammer using a repurposed luncheon meat can!
missions: Investigated various electronic jamming techniques ranging from dynamic barrage to swept frequency jamming.
Spearheaded the design of a novel antenna using a repurposed luncheon meat can as the waveguide to effectively propagate the jamming signals.
Leveraged state-of-the-art ADALM Pluto Software Defined Radios (SDRs) to generate powerful, precision-tuned jamming signals, ensuring optimal efficacy in disabling drone control links.
Successfully disrupted the control link between a Parrot Mambo drone and its controller (phone), validating the viability of our solution.

title: Student Researcher
quote: Took up this research opportunity as a high schooler and managed to find a mentor that reignited my interest in learning and programming!
missions: Investigated the approach for the characterisation, calibration, and compensation of channel mismatches in a Quadrature Modulated Waveform Generator (QMWG).
Error analysis was done using the Figure of Merit (FoM) as the performance metric.
Appropriate calibration and compensation were implemented and then tested using Python to confirm the effectiveness.
